note: From a verify pass, 2026-08-30, worked off data/research/luxembourg-city-staged.json (84 Wikidata candidates within 15km) plus the official INSPIRE geoportal export of Luxembourg's Reglement grand-ducal du 31 janvier 2025 (remarkable trees register, 238 national entries, 13 in the Luxembourg City commune). 4 trees verified to data/research/luxembourgcity-verified.json (lux_001 to lux_004). Only about a dozen of the 84 staged candidates were checked in the ~40 minute window; the rest (mostly outside the city core, in Hesperange, Kopstal, Walferdange, Bertrange, Leudelange, Contern, Niederanven etc, 3 to 15km out) were not reached at all and are neither leads nor blocked, just unchecked.

leads.name: Fagus sylvatica f. purpurea, near Lëtzebuerg City Museum
leads.reason: Register match found (INSPIRE point remarkable_trees.129, within ~1.3m), so this is very likely officially designated. Not verified further this pass due to the 4-candidate limit; a second, non-register source was not sought. Good candidate for a follow-up pass, in the same Ville-Haute cluster as lux_001/002/003.

About 1.75km from the Ville-Haute cluster in the Eich quarter. Worth a follow-up pass to firm up the register match and find a second source.

leads.reason: A named, historically/dynastically significant tree (planted for or named after Prince Charles of Luxembourg) close to the Ville-Haute cluster, but species and sourcing were not checked this pass; ran out of time within the 4-candidate limit.

blocked.name: Giant sequoia, Parc Amelie (Avenue Amelie)
blocked.reason: DEAD. This tree (Wikidata register ids 130 and 131, girth 895cm, height 36.8m, roughly 150 years old) matches the giant sequoia in Parc Amelie that Luxembourg City felled on 1 March 2026 after an Armillaria (honey fungus) infection made it unsafe, per Le Quotidien (lequotidien.lu/luxembourg/en-images-luxembourg-ville-le-sequoia-geant-de-150-ans-abattu/) and L'essentiel. A 38m crane was used; only the stump remains, part of the wood is being made into a memorial bench, and a replacement sequoia is planned. Never deliver as a live entry. Worth re-checking in a year or two in case the replacement planting becomes its own story, but that is a different, much younger tree.

blocked.name: Carpinus betulus (hornbeam, 'Hobich'), Kinnekswiss
blocked.reason: DEAD, standing as a snag. Per monumentaltrees.com (via search snippet, page itself Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch) this hornbeam, once the most photographed tree on the Kinnekswiss meadow and dating to the park's founding circa 1871, died in 2016 after consecutive hot summers plus two fungal pathogens. The city deliberately left the dead trunk standing as deadwood habitat rather than felling it, and planted new hornbeams in 2020 grown from its seed. Do not deliver as a living entry; the Wikidata record's 'age 150' and 2016 date-property are consistent with this being its death year, not a measurement year. A future pass could consider the 2020 seedling(s) once they are themselves identifiable and remarkable, but that is speculative and not something to chase now.
